title: Manuel Neuer extends Bayern Munich contract to 2027
content:
Manuel Neuer has extended his contract with Bayern Munich until 2027, keeping him at the German champions for a sixteenth year.

Neuer, 40, and has made 36 appearances this season, despite a three-week layoff due to a thigh injury, captaining the side on his way to a 13th Bundesliga title.

Bayern also confirmed that back-up goalkeeper Sven Ulreich had also signed a new deal until 2027.

On April 19, Vincent Kompany’s side won their 13th league title in 14 seasons, to add to their German Super Cup win. Bayern could still win a domestic treble, as they face Stuttgart in the DFB-Pokal final on May 23.

Neuer, whose contract was set to expire in the summer, has made 597 appearances for Bayern since joining from Schalke in 2011, winning 32 trophies and keeping 269 clean sheets in that time.

“I took my time over the decision and am now very happy,” he said. “Everything is just right here: with this team, we can beat anyone; I enjoy going to Sabener Strasse (Bayern’s training ground) every day and I’m performing to the best of my ability. In our goalkeeping team, we stick together and try to keep raising the bar, constantly pushing each other and preparing ourselves as well as possible for the games.”

The former Germany international has suffered seven severe muscle injuries since breaking his leg in December 2022, but has maintained his position as Bayern’s first-choice goalkeeper.

Neuer earned 124 caps for Germany, winning the World Cup in 2014, before retiring in 2024. In February, he ruled out the possibility of returning for this summer’s World Cup in the United States, Canada and Mexico.

Ulreich, 37, has had two different spells at Bayern, first joining in 2015 from Stuttgart. He started the majority of the 2017-18 season after Neuer suffered a metatarsal fracture. He left for Hamburg in 2020, though re-joined the club the following summer and has made 104 appearances across his two stints.

This season, he has mainly served as the third choice goalkeeper Jonas Urbig, who Bayern board member for sport, Max Eberl, said would be supported by Neuer and Ulreich on “on his path to becoming the future of FC Bayern”.
